why: The reference concept has a soft floor shadow under the bench and the Tier-1 foreground mask counts it (analysis/reference-suitability.md). Gate renders carry a matching contact shadow (an ambient-occlusion floor decal computed from the model's height above the floor, blurred; no light involved) so the silhouette comparison measures the same thing on both sides; the model's own lighting and key-light self-shadowing are unchanged.
how: Contact-shadow settings from shadow sweeps (renders/camera-fit/shadow-sweep.json: settings scored by Tier-1 IoU on the fixed view). The reference's floor shadow is darker in its core (L 60-76) than a faint IoU-optimal decal and is thrown a little behind the bench by the concept's frontal key, so the kept setting sits 15% of the footprint depth toward the back with a darker core: opacity 0.3 at the material pass, 0.36 at the surface pass and 0.45 from the optimization pass, each raised when lighter floor pixels split off as their own light-grey colour cluster (the reference's floor pixels share the blade's grey cluster). At 0.45 the render's five colour clusters are #9f6844 #979598 #3c261d #c6946c #673f2a against the reference's #966138 #8d8c8e #2e1d17 #bc8d65 #693e25, at IoU 0.874 (0.02 below the faintest decal's best).
allowHolesWhy: The bench frame encloses real negative spaces (under the top between the legs, stretchers and cross braces; declared in silhouetteAnalysis.negativeSpaces), so turntable views are holed by design.
exposureWhy: With the studio light at exposure 1.45 the material regions of the fixed view land within dE 3-6 of the reference's region means (bench front 3.2, blade 4.4, log side 5.6; _lib/region_compare.py) and the render's five colour clusters line up with the reference's.
fixedLightWhy: The concept is a product-style render: a soft overhead key, deep occlusion under the top (its darkest colour cluster is #2e1d17) and a frontal fill that lights the log's cut face. The game-like 'neutral' light lifts those darks with a strong hemisphere fill, so the fixed (gate) view uses the harness's 'studio' light; orbit views keep 'neutral' and the game keeps its own lights.
